question: What will be the highest observed water level (ft above MLLW) at NOAA's La Jolla, CA tide gauge (station 9410230) on November 26-27, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Value = predicted astronomical high (6.84 ft at 09:15 PST Nov 26, the higher of the two window highs) + non-tidal residual + small 6-min noise. NOAA API data show residual at highs of ~+1.4-1.56 ft on Nov 10-14, easing to ~+1.0-1.3 ft on Nov 15-18; calcoasttides cites +15.1 in (24h mean) as of Nov 17. The persistent El Nino/Kelvin-wave component makes ~1.2 ft the central residual -> ~8.05 ft. Upside: forecast storm systems (surge, wave setup), a new Kelvin pulse. Downside: further residual decay toward ~0.8 ft. The Polymarket La Jolla peak contracts close 2027-04-01 and are likely season-max contracts; terms could not be loaded (header overflow) and the prices are internally inconsistent, so they are treated as weak evidence, not an anchor.

calls.reasoning: Window max = Nov 26 09:15 PST high (pred 6.84 ft MLLW) + daily-max residual. Recent daily-max residuals Nov 14-18 are +1.44, +1.26, +1.26, ~+1.3, +1.15 (these already include 6-min noise), easing from +1.5 on Nov 12-13. Persistent El Nino/Kelvin-wave anomaly argues against fast decay; forecast storms and surf give upside skew. Median ~6.84+1.23 = 8.07, about the October record of ~7.97. calls.reconciliation: Main dispute was the residual to add: Run 2 used the Nov 1-13 mean (~1.4 ft), Runs 1 and 3 used recent values (1.0-1.3). The dossiers agree on Nov 14-18 daily-max residuals (1.44, 1.26, 1.26, ~1.3, 1.15), so the current level is ~1.25 and Run 2 is out of date. Runs 1 and 3 added 6-min noise on top of partly smooth or low-tide residuals, double-counting where they used daily-max numbers; the low-tide baseline of ~1.1 ft plus ~0.15 ft peak excess agrees with ~1.25. Decay versus storm upside is pure judgment: took a slight decay with upside skew. No web access this run; market terms unverifiable.
